subject: Commit onboarding staircase playbook and month-to-month step-ups
messages:
From: Samantha Glass <samantha.glass@brightline.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing + commit question for March launch

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to move from pilot to a broader launch target in June, but need clarity on how monthly commits and per-token discounts would scale during our ramp. A couple of things we need to lock down before procurement: 

- Example monthly step-up schedule for a six-month launch ramp (pilot -> 1M tokens -> 5M tokens).
- How seasonality is handled (we expect a spike in November).
- True-up mechanics vs credits if we under/over shoot a monthly commit.
- Any one-time launch credits for training & pre-warm traffic.

Can you share a concise proposal with concrete numbers? I attached our rough launch profile (launch_profile_estimates.xlsx).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that’s easier.

—Samantha
Samantha Glass
Head of Product, Brightline AI
Samantha.Glass@brightline.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment: launch_profile_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)

From: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Glass <samantha.glass@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing + commit question for March launch

Samantha —

Great to meet you yesterday; appreciate the launch profile. I reviewed the attachment and sketched a practical "staircase" commit playbook that balances your seasonality concerns with per-token economics. Attached is an initial proposal PDF (Brightline_commit_proposal_v2.pdf) and a CSV that maps monthly step-ups to estimated token usage and unit price. High-level summary: 

- Baseline: month 0 (pilot) -> 200k tokens (usage band 0-0.25M).
- Step-up cadence (example 6-month): 0.2M -> 1.0M -> 2.5M -> 3.5M -> 5.0M -> 6.5M.
- Per-token price tiers: 0-0.5M = $0.00012/token; 0.5-2.5M = $0.000095/token; 2.5-5M = $0.000075/token; 5M+ = $0.00006/token.
- First-month launch credit: 20% credit against committed spend (one-time, to cover pre-warm and eval).
- True-up: monthly true-up with a 10% seasonality buffer for months with large uncertainty (you pick which months to flag). Underspend is converted to a credit applied to next month; overspend billed at the tiered per-token overage rate.

I’ve looped in Ben (SE) for performance/throughput sizing and Monica (CS) for onboarding milestones. Karthik, can you confirm whether the tier breakpoints and first-month credit are feasible from a finance/renewal perspective?

If Brightline is happy with this shape, we can convert to a term sheet + a mutually agreeable true-up spreadsheet. Happy to run these numbers on a call — are you free Friday 10–11 PT?

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

Attachments: Brightline_commit_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 412KB); monthly_stepup_table.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing + commit question for March launch

Maya / team —

Quick pricing checks and recommended guardrails (internal):

- Tiers: the breakpoints you proposed are fine but suggest tightening the middle tier to 0.5-1.8M and adding a soft band 1.8-3.0M to smooth per-token cliffs for Brightline’s expected jump from 1M to 2.5M. That reduces churn risk when they cross thresholds mid-month.
- Seasonality buffer: recommend a 15% buffer for November (marketing peak). For other months a 10% buffer is reasonable.
- Credits/true-up: prefer an auto-credit model for underspend (credit applied next invoice) rather than refunds; finance likes that from a cashflow perspective. For overspend, bill at the next tier's per-token rate but cap effective price so Brightline never pays more than 5% above the committed blended rate in any one month (helps with procurement sign-off).
- First-month launch credit: agree to 20% but only if onboarding milestones (prewarm completed, one large integration test) are met. Otherwise reduce to 10%.

Operational notes for Ben: ensure we set up prefix caching and a conservative KV cache pre-warm during launch week; that reduces token consumption and can affect whether they hit higher tiers.

I can model three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) and export an updated monthly_stepup_table.csv with blended effective rates and cash impact.

Karthik
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

[Internal — do not forward]

Subject: Re: Initial pricing + commit question for March launch

Samantha —

Thanks for the profile and for the quick turnaround. I’ve attached an updated proposal that incorporates Karthik’s smoothing suggestion and the conditional first-month credit tied to onboarding milestones. High-level agreed points: 

- Proposed 6-month staircase commit (illustrative numbers in attached PDF).
- Tighter middle band (0.5–1.8M) and soft band to smooth cliffs.
- 20% one-time launch credit contingent on onboarding checklist (prewarm + integration test).
- 15% seasonality buffer for November; 10% default otherwise.
- Monthly true-up: underspend auto-credit; overspend billed at next-tier rate with a 5% cap on month-over-month effective price increase.

Next steps: 
1) Samantha / procurement to confirm they’re OK with the credit-conditional clause.
2) We’ll run the conservative/expected/aggressive scenarios and send the blended monthly cash projection by Monday.
3) If accepted, we’ll convert to a term sheet and route to legal for a short SOW addendum.

Would you like a 30-minute call Monday morning PT to walk the numbers?

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
